title: Final expression for E_p
description: Essential Criteria: The response must provide the correct approximate expression for the proton energy, E_p ≈ (m_Δ² - m_p²) / (4 E_b).

title: Conservation law application
description: Important Criteria: The solution must correctly apply both relativistic energy and momentum conservation to the head-on collision.

title: Ultrarelativistic approximation
description: Important Criteria: The reasoning must justify the approximation E_p ≈ p_p (or γ >> 1) for the proton, given that E_b is small.

title: Photon energy from wavelength
description: Essential Criteria: The calculation must correctly convert the given wavelength (1.06 mm) to a photon energy in eV using E = hc/λ.

title: Numerical proton energy
description: Essential Criteria: The final numerical answer for the proton energy must be correctly calculated from the given masses and the photon energy, resulting in an order of magnitude near 10^20 eV.

title: Algebraic manipulation
description: Important Criteria: The derivation should show correct algebraic steps combining the squared conservation equations and the energy-momentum relation.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional Criteria: The solution should demonstrate consistent handling of units, especially when converting between Joules and electron volts or using MeV/c² masses.

title: Neglecting E_b squared
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student incorrectly retains terms of order E_b² in the approximations, leading to an incorrect final expression.

title: Incorrect frame or sign
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the solution misapplies the head-on collision sign convention in momentum conservation or confuses laboratory and rest frames.
